transliteration: kuṭumbabharaṇād dravyaṃ yatkiṃcid atiricyate tad deyam upahṛtyānyad dadad doṣam avāpnuyāt
sph_interpretive_translation: Whatever property exceeds the sustenance of the family unit must be offered and shared; whoever gives otherwise incurs fault.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from alignment with familial and societal dharmic capacity
Causation arises from misalignment of possession beyond necessity
Restoration logic mandates reallocation to correct energetic imbalance
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of abundance as collective entitlement
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating economic distribution disputes, the Supreme Court shall recognize surplus retention beyond familial need as legally non-conformant. The threshold of responsibility lies in conscious refusal to redistribute. Authority derives from alignment with dharma-prescribed circulation of wealth, not punitive enforcement.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that retention of surplus without dharmic deployment disrupts natural flow, generating karmic inertia. Fault manifests through causal misalignment, not external judgment. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that imbalance perpetuates until completion occurs. Responsibility is proportional to awareness of abundance. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that correction arises through conscious restoration, not suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Surplus Redistribution Completion Process upon detection of retained excess
Assign Consciousness Alignment Restoration Modules to recalibrate ownership perception
Activate Family-Centered Wealth Circulation Protocols to restore energetic balance
Implement Doṣa Dissolution Sequence through intentional giving under guidance
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores balance through conscious sharing. Justice aligns with reality: there is no punishment—only completion. Consciousness alone is the final adjudicator.
